title: Call Him by His names
hookLine: the beautiful names again, in their home verse (7:180)

cards: On day two hundred thirty-two, this path opened the most beautiful names of Allah with the first half of this verse: the Merciful, the Forgiving, the Provider, the Patient.
Lists of names are lovely to read, and easy to treat like a museum, beautiful things behind glass. Today, the verse again, read all the way through, in its place in surah seven.
It says what the names are for, and then how they can be bent.

teach.h: FAD'UHU BIHA — CALL ON HIM BY THEM.
teach.b: Verse one-eighty, in Pickthall's words: “Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them.” In Arabic: wa lillahi al-asma' al-husna, fad'uhu biha. The word for call, ud'u, shares a root with du'a.
The names aren't only to know. They're to use, the way you use someone's name to get their attention.

teach.h: MATCH THE NAME TO THE NEED.
teach.b: So scholars teach matching the name to the need: when you need provision, ar-Razzaq, the Provider; when you've done wrong, al-Ghafur, the Forgiving; when you're afraid, as-Salam, Peace.
The verse goes on: leave those who distort His names.

The verb is yulhiduna, from a root meaning to swerve to one side. A Muslim grave may have a lahd, a niche dug into the side wall: the same root. To distort the names is to bend them away from what they mean.
A hadith in Bukhari says Allah has ninety-nine names, and whoever counts them will enter paradise; scholars explained count as learning, understanding and living by them.
But some scholars held that ninety-nine is not the limit, citing a du'a reported from the Prophet ﷺ that asks by every name Allah has named Himself, including those He kept hidden with Himself.
The list is a door, not the whole house. The phrase al-asma' al-husna appears in four places in the Qur'an. Here it comes with a plain command, and a warning.

how: Muslims often begin a du'a with the divine name that fits the request, such as ya Razzaq for provision or ya Ghafur for forgiveness, and some learn the ninety-nine names by heart.

o: the most beautiful names of Allah, to call Him by
the names of the angels who guard paradise
the ninety-nine prophets named in the Qur'an

games.q: match the name to the need — tap the pairs.

s: 7:180 tells believers to call on Allah by His names
fad'uhu biha: so call on Him by them.
all scholars hold there are exactly ninety-nine names
some cite a du'a asking by names Allah kept hidden, so ninety-nine is not the limit.
ilhad shares a root with the side niche of a grave
lahd: a niche dug to one side; ilhad, swerving aside.

games.q: you're anxious about money this month. 7:180 says call on Him by His names. which name fits best?
games.why: scholars teach matching the name to the need: ar-Razzaq for provision.

practice: Name to yourself one thing you need today, plainly: patience with a child, money for rent, courage for a conversation, rest. Pick the name that fits it, the Patient, the Provider, the Strong, Peace.
If you pray, call on Him by that name quietly, a few times with the breath; if you don't, sit with the name and the need side by side.
